clues.title: Statistical Ensembles & Partition Functions
clues.level1: Microcanonical ensemble: isolated system $(E, V, N)$ with entropy $S = k_B \ln \Omega(E)$. Temperature defined via $\frac{1}{T} = \left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial E}\right)_{V,N}$.
clues.level2: Canonical ensemble: system at fixed $(T, V, N)$. Boltzmann probability $P_i = \frac{e^{-\beta E_i}}{Z}$, with canonical partition function $Z = \sum_i e^{-\beta E_i}$ where $\beta = 1/(k_B T)$. Helmholtz free energy is $F = -k_B T \ln Z$.
clues.level3: Mean energy and fluctuations: $\langle E \rangle = -\frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial \beta} = k_B T^2 \frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial T}$. Heat capacity $C_v = \left(\frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial T}\right)_V = \frac{(\Delta E)^2}{k_B T^2} \geq 0$.
clues.level4: Equipartition Theorem: Every quadratic degree of freedom in the classical Hamiltonian contributes $\frac{1}{2}k_B T$ to mean energy and $\frac{1}{2}k_B$ to heat capacity.

clues.title: Central Potential & Keplerian Orbital Mechanics
clues.level1: In central potential $V(r)$, angular momentum $\vec{L} = \mu r^2 \dot{\theta} \hat{z}$ is strictly conserved, confining motion to a plane. Motion reduces to 1D via effective potential: $V_{\text{eff}}(r) = V(r) + \frac{L^2}{2\mu r^2}$.
clues.level2: Radial equation: $\mu\ddot{r} = -\frac{dV_{\text{eff}}}{dr} = F(r) + \frac{L^2}{\mu r^3}$. Circular orbit radius $r_0$ satisfies $\left.\frac{dV_{\text{eff}}}{dr}\right|_{r_0} = 0$, with stability condition $\left.\frac{d^2 V_{\text{eff}}}{dr^2}\right|_{r_0} > 0$.
clues.level3: Kepler orbit equation ($V = -k/r$): $r(\theta) = \frac{p}{1 + e\cos\theta}$, with semi-latus rectum $p = \frac{L^2}{\mu k}$ and eccentricity $e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{2EL^2}{\mu k^2}}$. ($e < 1 \implies$ ellipse, $e = 1 \implies$ parabola, $e > 1 \implies$ hyperbola).
clues.level4: Apsidal limits: At periapsis and apoapsis, $\dot{r} = 0$, so $E = V_{\text{eff}}(r_{\text{min}}) = V_{\text{eff}}(r_{\text{max}})$. Kepler's 3rd Law: $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{G(M+m)} a^3$.

clues.title: Rigid Body Mechanics & Rotational Dynamics
clues.level1: Angular momentum and angular velocity: $\vec{L} = \mathbf{I}\vec{\omega}$. Total kinetic energy: $T = \frac{1}{2}M v_{\text{CM}}^2 + \frac{1}{2}\vec{\omega}\cdot\mathbf{I}\vec{\omega}$.
clues.level2: Parallel Axis Theorem (Steiner): $I = I_{\text{CM}} + M d^2$. Pure rolling without slipping: $v_{\text{CM}} = R\omega$ and $a_{\text{CM}} = R\alpha$, with static friction providing torque $\tau = I\alpha$.
clues.level3: Euler's equations for principal axes: $I_1 \dot{\omega}_1 - (I_2 - I_3)\omega_2 \omega_3 = \tau_1$. For torque-free symmetric top ($I_1=I_2 \neq I_3$), precession frequency is $\Omega_{\text{prec}} = \frac{I_3 - I_1}{I_1}\omega_3$.
clues.level4: Standard inertia moments: Solid sphere $\frac{2}{5}MR^2$, spherical shell $\frac{2}{3}MR^2$, solid cylinder/disk $\frac{1}{2}MR^2$, thin rod $\frac{1}{12}ML^2$ (center) or $\frac{1}{3}ML^2$ (end).

clues.title: Lagrangian Mechanics & Generalized Coordinates
clues.level1: Identify the degrees of freedom and choose generalized coordinates $q_1, \dots, q_n$ matching geometric constraints. Form kinetic energy $T$ and potential energy $V$. The Lagrangian is $L(q, \dot{q}, t) = T - V$.
clues.level2: Euler-Lagrange equations: $\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_i}\right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_i} = 0$. If coordinate $q_k$ is cyclic (absent from $L$), conjugate momentum $p_k = \frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_k}$ is a conserved constant of motion.
clues.level3: Holonomic constraints $f(q_1,\dots,q_n)=0$: Use Lagrange multipliers $\lambda$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_i}\right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_i} = \lambda \frac{\partial f}{\partial q_i}$, where the RHS represents the generalized force of constraint.
clues.level4: Static equilibrium limit: When $\dot{q}_i = 0, \ddot{q}_i = 0$, equations reduce to $\frac{\partial V}{\partial q_i} = 0$. Verify dimensional consistency $[Q_i] = [\text{Work}]/[q_i]$.

clues.title: Hydrogen Atom & 3D Central Potentials
clues.level1: Coulomb potential $V(r) = -\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}$. Radial wave equation with centrifugal barrier: $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2\mu}\frac{d^2 u}{dr^2} + \left[V(r) + \frac{\hbar^2 l(l+1)}{2\mu r^2}\right]u = E u$.
clues.level2: Energy levels of Hydrogen: $E_n = -\frac{\mu e^4}{32\pi^2 \varepsilon_0^2 \hbar^2}\frac{1}{n^2} = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2}$, with Bohr radius $a_0 = \frac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 \hbar^2}{\mu e^2} \approx 0.529\text{ Å}$.
clues.level3: Quantum numbers: Principal $n=1,2,\dots$, orbital angular momentum $l=0,1,\dots,n-1$, magnetic $m=-l,\dots,+l$. Degeneracy of $n$-th energy level (without spin) is $n^2$, or $2n^2$ with spin.
clues.level4: Muonic atom scaling: If electron is replaced by muon of mass $m_\mu \approx 207 m_e$, orbital radii scale as $r_\mu = a_0/207$ and binding energies scale as $E_\mu = 207 E_e$.

clues.title: Photoelectric Effect & Photon-Matter Interactions
clues.level1: Einstein's photoelectric equation: $K_{\text{max}} = h\nu - \Phi = \frac{h c}{\lambda} - \Phi = e V_s$, where $\Phi$ is the work function and $V_s$ is the stopping potential.
clues.level2: Cutoff threshold: Photoemission occurs only if frequency exceeds cutoff $\nu_0 = \Phi/h$ (or wavelength $\lambda \leq \lambda_0 = hc/\Phi$), independent of light intensity.
clues.level3: Compton scattering of photon on stationary electron: Wavelength shift is $\Delta \lambda = \lambda' - \lambda = \lambda_c(1 - \cos\theta)$, where Compton wavelength is $\lambda_c = \frac{h}{m_e c} \approx 2.43 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m} = 0.0243\text{ Å}$.
clues.level4: Photon momentum: $\vec{p} = \hbar\vec{k} = \frac{h}{\lambda}\hat{n}$, photon energy $E = h\nu = \hbar\omega$. Relativistic momentum conservation governs Compton collision.

clues.title: Thermodynamic Laws & Heat Engine Cycles
clues.level1: 1st Law: $dU = \delta Q - \delta W$. Work done by gas is $W = \int p dV$. For ideal gas, internal energy depends solely on temperature: $dU = n C_V dT$.
clues.level2: 2nd Law: Efficiency of any heat engine operating between $T_H$ and $T_C$ is $\eta = \frac{W}{Q_H} = 1 - \frac{Q_C}{Q_H} \leq \eta_{\text{Carnot}} = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$.
clues.level3: Adiabatic processes ($dQ=0$): $p V^\gamma = \text{const}$, $T V^{\gamma-1} = \text{const}$, where $\gamma = C_p/C_v = 1 + 2/d$ ($d=3 \implies \gamma = 5/3$, $d=5 \implies \gamma = 7/5$).
clues.level4: Entropy changes: $\Delta S = \int \frac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T}$. For ideal gas: $\Delta S = n C_v \ln(T_f/T_i) + nR \ln(V_f/V_i)$. In an isolated system, $\Delta S_{\text{univ}} \geq 0$ strictly.

clues.title: Dielectrics, Bound Charges & Capacitance
clues.level1: In linear isotropic dielectrics: electric displacement is $\vec{D} = \varepsilon_0 \vec{E} + \vec{P} = \varepsilon_r \varepsilon_0 \vec{E} = \varepsilon \vec{E}$. Gauss's Law for displacement depends solely on free charge: $\oint \vec{D}\cdot d\vec{A} = Q_{\text{free, enc}}$.
clues.level2: Bound polarization charges: volume density $\rho_b = -\nabla \cdot \vec{P}$ and surface density $\sigma_b = \vec{P}\cdot\hat{n}$. Capacitance increases by dielectric constant: $C = \kappa C_0 = \varepsilon_r C_0$.
clues.level3: Stored electrostatic energy: $U = \frac{1}{2} C V^2 = \frac{Q^2}{2C} = \frac{1}{2}\int \vec{D}\cdot\vec{E} d^3 r$.
clues.level4: Dielectric force check: Force on a dielectric slab partially inserted into a capacitor: at fixed voltage $F = +\frac{1}{2}V^2 \frac{dC}{dx}$ (attractive); at fixed charge $F = -\frac{1}{2}Q^2 \frac{d(1/C)}{dx}$.

clues.title: Poynting Vector, Energy Flux & EM Wave Propagation
clues.level1: Poynting Vector: $\vec{S} = \frac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec{E} \times \vec{B})$ represents instantaneous electromagnetic power flow per unit area $(\text{W/m}^2)$.
clues.level2: Monochromatic plane wave: $\vec{E} = E_0 \cos(\vec{k}\cdot\vec{r} - \omega t)\hat{n}$, $\vec{B} = \frac{1}{c}\hat{k} \times \vec{E}$. Time-averaged intensity is $\langle S \rangle = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 c E_0^2 = \frac{E_0^2}{2\mu_0 c}$.
clues.level3: Energy density of EM field: $u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 + \frac{1}{2\mu_0} B^2 = \varepsilon_0 E^2$. Total energy transport satisfies continuity $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \vec{S} = -\vec{J}\cdot\vec{E}$.
clues.level4: Radiation pressure: For total absorption $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{\langle S \rangle}{c}$; for total reflection $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{2\langle S \rangle}{c}$.

clues.title: Dirac Bra-Ket Formalism & Observable Operators
clues.level1: States are vectors $|\psi\rangle$ in Hilbert space with inner product $\langle\phi|\psi\rangle = \langle\psi|\phi\rangle^*$. Physical observables correspond to Hermitian operators $\hat{A} = \hat{A}^\dagger$ with real eigenvalues $a_n$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $\sum_n |n\rangle\langle n| = \mathbf{1}$.
clues.level2: Measurement postulate: Probability of measuring eigenvalue $a_n$ on state $|\psi\rangle$ is $P(a_n) = |\langle n|\psi\rangle|^2$. Expectation value is $\langle A \rangle = \langle\psi|\hat{A}|\psi\rangle$. Variance is $(\Delta A)^2 = \langle A^2 \rangle - \langle A \rangle^2$.
clues.level3: Generalized Uncertainty Principle: $\Delta A \Delta B \geq \frac{1}{2}|\langle [\hat{A}, \hat{B}] \rangle|$. Canonical commutator $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ implies $\Delta x \Delta p \geq \frac{\hbar}{2}$.
clues.level4: Time evolution: In Schrödinger picture, $|\psi(t)\rangle = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}|\psi(0)\rangle$. In Heisenberg picture, operators evolve via $\frac{d\hat{A}}{dt} = \frac{i}{\hbar}[\hat{H}, \hat{A}] + \frac{\partial\hat{A}}{\partial t}$ (Ehrenfest Theorem).

clues.title: Statistical Ensembles & Partition Functions
clues.level1: Microcanonical ensemble: isolated system $(E, V, N)$ with entropy $S = k_B \ln \Omega(E)$. Temperature defined via $\frac{1}{T} = \left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial E}\right)_{V,N}$.
clues.level2: Canonical ensemble: system at fixed $(T, V, N)$. Boltzmann probability $P_i = \frac{e^{-\beta E_i}}{Z}$, with canonical partition function $Z = \sum_i e^{-\beta E_i}$ where $\beta = 1/(k_B T)$. Helmholtz free energy is $F = -k_B T \ln Z$.
clues.level3: Mean energy and fluctuations: $\langle E \rangle = -\frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial \beta} = k_B T^2 \frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial T}$. Heat capacity $C_v = \left(\frac{\partial \langle E \rangle}{\partial T}\right)_V = \frac{(\Delta E)^2}{k_B T^2} \geq 0$.
clues.level4: Equipartition Theorem: Every quadratic degree of freedom in the classical Hamiltonian contributes $\frac{1}{2}k_B T$ to mean energy and $\frac{1}{2}k_B$ to heat capacity.

clues.title: Central Potential & Keplerian Orbital Mechanics
clues.level1: In central potential $V(r)$, angular momentum $\vec{L} = \mu r^2 \dot{\theta} \hat{z}$ is strictly conserved, confining motion to a plane. Motion reduces to 1D via effective potential: $V_{\text{eff}}(r) = V(r) + \frac{L^2}{2\mu r^2}$.
clues.level2: Radial equation: $\mu\ddot{r} = -\frac{dV_{\text{eff}}}{dr} = F(r) + \frac{L^2}{\mu r^3}$. Circular orbit radius $r_0$ satisfies $\left.\frac{dV_{\text{eff}}}{dr}\right|_{r_0} = 0$, with stability condition $\left.\frac{d^2 V_{\text{eff}}}{dr^2}\right|_{r_0} > 0$.
clues.level3: Kepler orbit equation ($V = -k/r$): $r(\theta) = \frac{p}{1 + e\cos\theta}$, with semi-latus rectum $p = \frac{L^2}{\mu k}$ and eccentricity $e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{2EL^2}{\mu k^2}}$. ($e < 1 \implies$ ellipse, $e = 1 \implies$ parabola, $e > 1 \implies$ hyperbola).
clues.level4: Apsidal limits: At periapsis and apoapsis, $\dot{r} = 0$, so $E = V_{\text{eff}}(r_{\text{min}}) = V_{\text{eff}}(r_{\text{max}})$. Kepler's 3rd Law: $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{G(M+m)} a^3$.

clues.title: Rigid Body Mechanics & Rotational Dynamics
clues.level1: Angular momentum and angular velocity: $\vec{L} = \mathbf{I}\vec{\omega}$. Total kinetic energy: $T = \frac{1}{2}M v_{\text{CM}}^2 + \frac{1}{2}\vec{\omega}\cdot\mathbf{I}\vec{\omega}$.

clues.level3: Euler's equations for principal axes: $I_1 \dot{\omega}_1 - (I_2 - I_3)\omega_2 \omega_3 = \tau_1$. For torque-free symmetric top ($I_1=I_2 \neq I_3$), precession frequency is $\Omega_{\text{prec}} = \frac{I_3 - I_1}{I_1}\omega_3$.

clues.title: Lagrangian Mechanics & Generalized Coordinates
clues.level1: Identify the degrees of freedom and choose generalized coordinates $q_1, \dots, q_n$ matching geometric constraints. Form kinetic energy $T$ and potential energy $V$. The Lagrangian is $L(q, \dot{q}, t) = T - V$.
clues.level2: Euler-Lagrange equations: $\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_i}\right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_i} = 0$. If coordinate $q_k$ is cyclic (absent from $L$), conjugate momentum $p_k = \frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_k}$ is a conserved constant of motion.
clues.level3: Holonomic constraints $f(q_1,\dots,q_n)=0$: Use Lagrange multipliers $\lambda$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_i}\right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_i} = \lambda \frac{\partial f}{\partial q_i}$, where the RHS represents the generalized force of constraint.
clues.level4: Static equilibrium limit: When $\dot{q}_i = 0, \ddot{q}_i = 0$, equations reduce to $\frac{\partial V}{\partial q_i} = 0$. Verify dimensional consistency $[Q_i] = [\text{Work}]/[q_i]$.

clues.title: Matter Waves & Wave-Particle Duality
clues.level1: de Broglie relation: A particle of momentum $p = mv$ possesses an associated matter wavelength $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{mv}$.
clues.level2: Non-relativistic particle with kinetic energy $K = \frac{p^2}{2m} = q V$: de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m K}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m q V}}$. For electron: $\lambda \approx \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ Å}$.
clues.level3: Bragg diffraction of matter waves on crystal lattices with atomic spacing $d$: Constructive interference condition is $2d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ (Davisson-Germer experiment).
clues.level4: Phase and group velocity: Phase velocity $v_{\text{ph}} = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{E}{p} = \frac{c^2}{v} > c$; Group velocity of wave packet $v_g = \frac{d\omega}{dk} = \frac{dE}{dp} = v$ equals the physical particle speed.

clues.title: Photoelectric Effect & Photon-Matter Interactions
clues.level1: Einstein's photoelectric equation: $K_{\text{max}} = h\nu - \Phi = \frac{h c}{\lambda} - \Phi = e V_s$, where $\Phi$ is the work function and $V_s$ is the stopping potential.
clues.level2: Cutoff threshold: Photoemission occurs only if frequency exceeds cutoff $\nu_0 = \Phi/h$ (or wavelength $\lambda \leq \lambda_0 = hc/\Phi$), independent of light intensity.
clues.level3: Compton scattering of photon on stationary electron: Wavelength shift is $\Delta \lambda = \lambda' - \lambda = \lambda_c(1 - \cos\theta)$, where Compton wavelength is $\lambda_c = \frac{h}{m_e c} \approx 2.43 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m} = 0.0243\text{ Å}$.
clues.level4: Photon momentum: $\vec{p} = \hbar\vec{k} = \frac{h}{\lambda}\hat{n}$, photon energy $E = h\nu = \hbar\omega$. Relativistic momentum conservation governs Compton collision.

clues.title: Angular Momentum & Spin-1/2 Algebra
clues.level1: Angular momentum commutator algebra: $[\hat{J}_i, \hat{J}_j] = i\hbar \varepsilon_{ijk}\hat{J}_k$. Simultaneous eigenbasis $|j, m\rangle$ satisfies $\hat{J}^2|j, m\rangle = \hbar^2 j(j+1)|j, m\rangle$ and $\hat{J}_z|j, m\rangle = \hbar m|j, m\rangle$, with $-j \leq m \leq j$.
clues.level2: Ladder operators $\hat{J}_\pm = \hat{J}_x \pm i\hat{J}_y$ act as $\hat{J}_\pm|j, m\rangle = \hbar\sqrt{j(j+1) - m(m\pm 1)}|j, m\pm 1\rangle$.
clues.level3: Spin-1/2 ($s=1/2$): $\vec{S} = \frac{\hbar}{2}\vec{\sigma}$, where Pauli matrices are $\sigma_x = \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_y = \begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_z = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Note $\sigma_i^2 = \mathbf{1}$ and $\{\sigma_i, \sigma_j\} = 2\delta_{ij}$.
clues.level4: Addition of angular momenta $j_1 \otimes j_2$: Total angular momentum takes values $|j_1 - j_2| \leq J \leq j_1 + j_2$ in integer steps. Singlet state ($J=0$) is antisymmetric $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|\uparrow\downarrow\rangle - |\downarrow\uparrow\rangle)$, triplet ($J=1$) is symmetric.

clues.title: Continuous Charge Distributions & Electric Field/Potential Integrals
clues.level1: Divide the continuous geometry into differential charge elements $dq = \lambda dl'$ (line), $\sigma dA'$ (surface), or $\rho dV'$ (volume). Potential is $V(\vec{r}) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int \frac{dq}{|\vec{r} - \vec{r}'|}$ and electric field is $\vec{E}(\vec{r}) = -\nabla V$.
clues.level2: Exploit geometric symmetry: On symmetry axes (e.g. $z$-axis of a ring of radius $R$ carrying charge $Q$), transverse field components cancel symmetrically ($E_x = E_y = 0$). The axial field is $E_z = \frac{Q z}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (z^2 + R^2)^{3/2}}$.
clues.level3: For disk of radius $R$ with surface charge $\sigma$: $E_z = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 - \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^2 + R^2}}\right)$. For infinite plane ($R \to \infty$), field becomes uniform $E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$.
clues.level4: Asymptotic dipole and monopole checks: For $z \gg R$, expand $(1 + R^2/z^2)^{-3/2} \approx 1 - \frac{3}{2}\frac{R^2}{z^2}$, recovering the point-charge Coulomb field $E_z \to \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 z^2}$.

clues.title: Poynting Vector, Energy Flux & EM Wave Propagation
clues.level1: Poynting Vector: $\vec{S} = \frac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec{E} \times \vec{B})$ represents instantaneous electromagnetic power flow per unit area $(\text{W/m}^2)$.
clues.level2: Monochromatic plane wave: $\vec{E} = E_0 \cos(\vec{k}\cdot\vec{r} - \omega t)\hat{n}$, $\vec{B} = \frac{1}{c}\hat{k} \times \vec{E}$. Time-averaged intensity is $\langle S \rangle = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 c E_0^2 = \frac{E_0^2}{2\mu_0 c}$.
clues.level3: Energy density of EM field: $u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 + \frac{1}{2\mu_0} B^2 = \varepsilon_0 E^2$. Total energy transport satisfies continuity $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \vec{S} = -\vec{J}\cdot\vec{E}$.
clues.level4: Radiation pressure: For total absorption $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{\langle S \rangle}{c}$; for total reflection $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{2\langle S \rangle}{c}$.

clues.title: Small Oscillations, Secular Matrix & Normal Modes
clues.level1: Taylor expansion about stable equilibrium $q_0$: $V(q) \approx V(q_0) + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j} V_{ij} \eta_i \eta_j$, where $V_{ij} = \left.\frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial q_i \partial q_j}\right|_{q_0}$ and $\eta_i = q_i - q_{0,i}$. Kinetic energy is $T = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j} T_{ij} \dot{\eta}_i \dot{\eta}_j$.
clues.level2: Secular equation: $\det(\mathbf{V} - \omega^2 \mathbf{T}) = 0$. The roots $\omega_k^2$ are the squared normal mode frequencies.
clues.level3: Normal mode eigenvectors satisfy $(\mathbf{V} - \omega_k^2 \mathbf{T})\vec{a}^{(k)} = 0$. General motion is superposition: $\vec{\eta}(t) = \sum_k C_k \vec{a}^{(k)}\cos(\omega_k t + \phi_k)$.
clues.level4: Symmetry check: In symmetric systems (e.g. coupled pendula), symmetric mode has equal displacements $\eta_1 = \eta_2$ (spring at rest), while antisymmetric mode has $\eta_1 = -\eta_2$ (spring maximum stretch).

clues.title: Dirac Bra-Ket Formalism & Observable Operators
clues.level1: States are vectors $|\psi\rangle$ in Hilbert space with inner product $\langle\phi|\psi\rangle = \langle\psi|\phi\rangle^*$. Physical observables correspond to Hermitian operators $\hat{A} = \hat{A}^\dagger$ with real eigenvalues $a_n$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $\sum_n |n\rangle\langle n| = \mathbf{1}$.
clues.level2: Measurement postulate: Probability of measuring eigenvalue $a_n$ on state $|\psi\rangle$ is $P(a_n) = |\langle n|\psi\rangle|^2$. Expectation value is $\langle A \rangle = \langle\psi|\hat{A}|\psi\rangle$. Variance is $(\Delta A)^2 = \langle A^2 \rangle - \langle A \rangle^2$.
clues.level3: Generalized Uncertainty Principle: $\Delta A \Delta B \geq \frac{1}{2}|\langle [\hat{A}, \hat{B}] \rangle|$. Canonical commutator $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ implies $\Delta x \Delta p \geq \frac{\hbar}{2}$.
clues.level4: Time evolution: In Schrödinger picture, $|\psi(t)\rangle = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}|\psi(0)\rangle$. In Heisenberg picture, operators evolve via $\frac{d\hat{A}}{dt} = \frac{i}{\hbar}[\hat{H}, \hat{A}] + \frac{\partial\hat{A}}{\partial t}$ (Ehrenfest Theorem).

clues.title: Thermodynamic Laws & Heat Engine Cycles
clues.level1: 1st Law: $dU = \delta Q - \delta W$. Work done by gas is $W = \int p dV$. For ideal gas, internal energy depends solely on temperature: $dU = n C_V dT$.
clues.level2: 2nd Law: Efficiency of any heat engine operating between $T_H$ and $T_C$ is $\eta = \frac{W}{Q_H} = 1 - \frac{Q_C}{Q_H} \leq \eta_{\text{Carnot}} = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H}$.
clues.level3: Adiabatic processes ($dQ=0$): $p V^\gamma = \text{const}$, $T V^{\gamma-1} = \text{const}$, where $\gamma = C_p/C_v = 1 + 2/d$ ($d=3 \implies \gamma = 5/3$, $d=5 \implies \gamma = 7/5$).
clues.level4: Entropy changes: $\Delta S = \int \frac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T}$. For ideal gas: $\Delta S = n C_v \ln(T_f/T_i) + nR \ln(V_f/V_i)$. In an isolated system, $\Delta S_{\text{univ}} \geq 0$ strictly.

clues.title: Central Potential & Keplerian Orbital Mechanics
clues.level1: In central potential $V(r)$, angular momentum $\vec{L} = \mu r^2 \dot{\theta} \hat{z}$ is strictly conserved, confining motion to a plane. Motion reduces to 1D via effective potential: $V_{\text{eff}}(r) = V(r) + \frac{L^2}{2\mu r^2}$.
clues.level2: Radial equation: $\mu\ddot{r} = -\frac{dV_{\text{eff}}}{dr} = F(r) + \frac{L^2}{\mu r^3}$. Circular orbit radius $r_0$ satisfies $\left.\frac{dV_{\text{eff}}}{dr}\right|_{r_0} = 0$, with stability condition $\left.\frac{d^2 V_{\text{eff}}}{dr^2}\right|_{r_0} > 0$.
clues.level3: Kepler orbit equation ($V = -k/r$): $r(\theta) = \frac{p}{1 + e\cos\theta}$, with semi-latus rectum $p = \frac{L^2}{\mu k}$ and eccentricity $e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{2EL^2}{\mu k^2}}$. ($e < 1 \implies$ ellipse, $e = 1 \implies$ parabola, $e > 1 \implies$ hyperbola).
clues.level4: Apsidal limits: At periapsis and apoapsis, $\dot{r} = 0$, so $E = V_{\text{eff}}(r_{\text{min}}) = V_{\text{eff}}(r_{\text{max}})$. Kepler's 3rd Law: $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{G(M+m)} a^3$.

clues.title: Newtonian Dynamics & Non-Inertial Rotating Frames
clues.level1: Newton's Second Law: $\sum \vec{F} = m\vec{a}$. For circular motion of radius $R$ at speed $v$, centripetal acceleration is $a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} = \omega^2 R$.

clues.level1: de Broglie relation: A particle of momentum $p = mv$ possesses an associated matter wavelength $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{mv}$.

clues.title: Continuous Charge Distributions & Electric Field/Potential Integrals
clues.level1: Divide the continuous geometry into differential charge elements $dq = \lambda dl'$ (line), $\sigma dA'$ (surface), or $\rho dV'$ (volume). Potential is $V(\vec{r}) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int \frac{dq}{|\vec{r} - \vec{r}'|}$ and electric field is $\vec{E}(\vec{r}) = -\nabla V$.
clues.level2: Exploit geometric symmetry: On symmetry axes (e.g. $z$-axis of a ring of radius $R$ carrying charge $Q$), transverse field components cancel symmetrically ($E_x = E_y = 0$). The axial field is $E_z = \frac{Q z}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (z^2 + R^2)^{3/2}}$.
clues.level3: For disk of radius $R$ with surface charge $\sigma$: $E_z = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 - \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^2 + R^2}}\right)$. For infinite plane ($R \to \infty$), field becomes uniform $E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$.
clues.level4: Asymptotic dipole and monopole checks: For $z \gg R$, expand $(1 + R^2/z^2)^{-3/2} \approx 1 - \frac{3}{2}\frac{R^2}{z^2}$, recovering the point-charge Coulomb field $E_z \to \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 z^2}$.

clues.title: Poynting Vector, Energy Flux & EM Wave Propagation
clues.level1: Poynting Vector: $\vec{S} = \frac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec{E} \times \vec{B})$ represents instantaneous electromagnetic power flow per unit area $(\text{W/m}^2)$.
clues.level2: Monochromatic plane wave: $\vec{E} = E_0 \cos(\vec{k}\cdot\vec{r} - \omega t)\hat{n}$, $\vec{B} = \frac{1}{c}\hat{k} \times \vec{E}$. Time-averaged intensity is $\langle S \rangle = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 c E_0^2 = \frac{E_0^2}{2\mu_0 c}$.
clues.level3: Energy density of EM field: $u = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 + \frac{1}{2\mu_0} B^2 = \varepsilon_0 E^2$. Total energy transport satisfies continuity $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot \vec{S} = -\vec{J}\cdot\vec{E}$.
clues.level4: Radiation pressure: For total absorption $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{\langle S \rangle}{c}$; for total reflection $P_{\text{rad}} = \frac{2\langle S \rangle}{c}$.

clues.title: Conductors, Cavities & Electrostatic Shielding
clues.level1: In electrostatic equilibrium: electric field inside a conductor is zero ($ec{E} = 0$), the entire conductor is an equipotential ($V = \text{const}$), and net free charge resides exclusively on exterior surfaces.
clues.level2: Cavity with enclosed charge $q$: By Gauss's law around the cavity, an induced charge $-q$ distributes on the inner cavity wall to ensure $\vec{E} = 0$ in the bulk. An equal $+q$ appears on the outer surface.
clues.level3: Grounded conductor: Setting $V = 0$ at the outer surface removes exterior fields caused by interior charges, achieving complete electrostatic shielding (Faraday cage).
clues.level4: Electrostatic pressure: The outward repulsive force on the surface of a charged conductor is $P = \frac{\sigma^2}{2\varepsilon_0} = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_{\text{surf}}^2$.

clues.title: Work-Energy Theorem & 1D Potential Energy Curves
clues.level1: Work-Energy Theorem: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K = \frac{1}{2}m v_f^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v_i^2$. For conservative forces $F(x) = -\frac{dV}{dx}$, total mechanical energy $E = K + V(x)$ is conserved.
clues.level2: 1D motion analysis: $v(x) = \pm \sqrt{\frac{2}{m}(E - V(x))}$. Turning points occur where $E = V(x) \implies v = 0$. Motion is bounded in intervals where $E \geq V(x)$.
clues.level3: Period of 1D periodic motion: $T = 2\int_{x_{\text{min}}}^{x_{\text{max}}} \frac{dx}{\sqrt{\frac{2}{m}(E - V(x))}}$.
clues.level4: Equilibrium stability: $\left.\frac{dV}{dx}\right|_{x_0} = 0$. Stable if $\left.\frac{d^2 V}{dx^2}\right|_{x_0} > 0$ (oscillation frequency $\omega = \sqrt{V''(x_0)/m}$), unstable if $V''(x_0) < 0$.

clues.title: Dirac Bra-Ket Formalism & Observable Operators
clues.level1: States are vectors $|\psi\rangle$ in Hilbert space with inner product $\langle\phi|\psi\rangle = \langle\psi|\phi\rangle^*$. Physical observables correspond to Hermitian operators $\hat{A} = \hat{A}^\dagger$ with real eigenvalues $a_n$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $\sum_n |n\rangle\langle n| = \mathbf{1}$.
clues.level2: Measurement postulate: Probability of measuring eigenvalue $a_n$ on state $|\psi\rangle$ is $P(a_n) = |\langle n|\psi\rangle|^2$. Expectation value is $\langle A \rangle = \langle\psi|\hat{A}|\psi\rangle$. Variance is $(\Delta A)^2 = \langle A^2 \rangle - \langle A \rangle^2$.
clues.level3: Generalized Uncertainty Principle: $\Delta A \Delta B \geq \frac{1}{2}|\langle [\hat{A}, \hat{B}] \rangle|$. Canonical commutator $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ implies $\Delta x \Delta p \geq \frac{\hbar}{2}$.
clues.level4: Time evolution: In Schrödinger picture, $|\psi(t)\rangle = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}|\psi(0)\rangle$. In Heisenberg picture, operators evolve via $\frac{d\hat{A}}{dt} = \frac{i}{\hbar}[\hat{H}, \hat{A}] + \frac{\partial\hat{A}}{\partial t}$ (Ehrenfest Theorem).

clues.title: Entropy Calculations & Irreversible Processes
clues.level1: Entropy differential: $dS = \frac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T}$. For any irreversible process between initial state $i$ and final state $f$, $\Delta S = \int_i^f \frac{dQ_{\text{rev}}}{T}$ calculated along an arbitrary reversible path.
clues.level2: Free adiabatic expansion into vacuum (Joule expansion): No work is done ($W=0$) and no heat is exchanged ($Q=0$), so $\Delta U = 0 \implies T_f = T_i$ (ideal gas). Entropy change is $\Delta S = n R \ln(V_f/V_i) > 0$.
clues.level3: Thermal contact between two bodies ($T_1, T_2$) with heat capacity $C$: Final temperature is $T_f = \frac{T_1 + T_2}{2}$. Total entropy change is $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = C \ln\left(\frac{T_f^2}{T_1 T_2}\right) \geq 0$.
clues.level4: Statistical definition: Boltzmann entropy $S = k_B \ln \Omega$. 2nd Law states the number of accessible microstates $\Omega$ cannot decrease in an isolated system.
